chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The child stands to the right of the man in prayer when a group has arranged the row, and the seated patient stands to the right of the child when a group has arranged the row.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Qasabani and Ayub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from al-Arjami, from his father, who raised the hadith to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:
'Whoever leads a people in prayer while among them is one who is more knowledgeable than him, their affair will remain in decline until the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the standing positions of children and patients in congregational prayer, and what is the ruling if a less knowledgeable person leads a more knowledgeable one?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the hierarchical arrangement of the prayer row (saff), placing children and the seated ill to the right of the adult male, reflecting the Shia emphasis on order and respect in communal worship. It further establishes a critical criterion for imamate: leading those superior in knowledge leads to spiritual decline, underscoring the principle that religious authority is tied to scholarly merit (ilm) rather than mere seniority.
